label: external liquidity aggregator
summary: Plan a hook that sources or settles liquidity through exact external protocol adapters without hiding routing, reserves, or failure dependencies.
requiredFacts: Exact supported external protocols, adapter source and runtime identities, pool or market ids, currencies, fees and authorization
Deterministic adapter selection that never treats an address prefix, byte pattern, metadata label or caller assertion as authority
Quote, route, callback, hookData, sender, slippage, deadline, partial fill, settlement and refund parity across both systems
Reserve and liability model before, during and after external calls, including reentrancy and callback-capable tokens
Failure isolation, adapter disablement, upgrade, monitoring, user exit and public dependency disclosures
requiredFiles: Pinned hook, adapter and external protocol interface closure
Per-adapter integration, fork and failure tests
requiredTests: Address-prefix collisions, wrong adapter, wrong pool, wrong currency, unauthorized registry change and malicious metadata
All swap quadrants, partial fills, price limits, hookData, sender changes and final cross-protocol balances
External revert, reentrancy, pause, upgrade, fee change, stale state, insufficient liquidity and malformed return data
Adapter disablement, refund, rescue, retirement and user exit without trapped or cross-pool funds
Quoter, router, onchain trace and indexed event parity for every supported adapter
risks: Every adapter imports the external protocol's upgrade, liquidity, fee, callback and governance risks
Heuristic adapter identities can collide and route value into an unintended implementation
Cross-protocol partial failure can leave misleading quotes, trapped inventory or insolvent liabilities
